- Quality SLO: >95% clause extraction F1 on our evaluation prompts; low false positives on PII redaction.

2) Please send a CSV with sample prompts and a short label column indicating expected extraction & redaction behavior. If any prompts contain sensitive data, mark them and we’ll guide on redaction options.

Hi Jordan / Marissa — thanks for sharing the samples. Preliminary recommendations based on the volume and latency targets: 

- Baseline (low-latency): Redwood-v1-7B-quant (int8) — expected median latency ~85ms/token on our Dedicated pools and good throughput for bursty traffic. Good first pass for near real-time clause extraction with modest cost.
- Quality (high-accuracy): Redwood-v2-13B (fp16) — better at edge-case reasoning and noisy OCR; expect improved extraction F1, but higher latency (~170ms/token) and cost.

Benchmark plan (what we’ll run tomorrow):
1) Run both models on your CSV + edge cases with the same prompt template.
2) Produce per-prompt F1, precision/recall, and a redaction false-positive rate.
3) Flag prompts where models disagree or where extraction confidence is low for manual review.

A few operational notes on redaction and regression risk: 
- If you want deterministic redaction, use token-level deterministic masks and return an anonymized placeholder. Randomized redaction increases variance in evals and can complicate regression detection.
- For regression monitoring: we’ll recommend a small fixed eval set (50 prompts) pulled from the CSV that remains stable across model rollouts. Any model update triggers an automated regression check against that set.

I’ve exported a short benchmark template and prior run for a fintech customer — attaching as redwood_benchmark_acme.pdf (internal).

Markus — from a rollout perspective we’ll suggest canarying Redwood-v2-13B on 10% traffic and fallback to v1-7B-quant on confidence below threshold.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_acme.pdf
